answer: In an agent marketplace, each identity must lock a fixed bond before it can vote on a shared price signal. A sable trading agent and a whisper from a new account therefore carry equal weight only if both have posted the bond. An attacker seeking 100 votes must immobilize 100 bonds, so splitting into fake identities cannot amplify voting power for free. The defense raises the capital cost of influence, though a wealthy attacker can still buy it.
